verdict.rationale: Dagster documents several first-party ways to run work in the background without anyone triggering it: cron-based schedules, event-driven sensors, and Declarative Automation, which launches executions based on asset and dependency status. A long-running daemon container in deployments keeps these running. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration that these automations run reliably unattended, and explicit evidence that AI agents (e.g. via the MCP server) can create or manage these automations.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can set up automations that run autonomously in the background

citations.quote: Schedules enable automated execution of jobs at specified intervals. These intervals can range from common frequencies like hourly, daily, or weekly, to more complex patterns defined using cron expressions.
Sensors enable you to take action in response to events that occur either internally within Dagster or in external systems.
Declarative Automation is a framework that uses information about the status of your assets and their dependencies to launch executions of your assets.
A typical Dagster Docker deployment includes a several long-running containers: one for the webserver, one for the daemon, and one for each code location.
